one_paragraph_summary: Tourism is the world's biggest industry (1 billion tourists, $1 trillion in 2010), and Malaysia -- with 23.6 million visitors spending $30 billion -- outearns the Philippines tenfold despite similar attractions; Malaysia's tourism receipts even exceed PH's total OFW remittances of $18.7 billion. Panganiban prescribes five fundamentals for transforming the Philippines into a tourism multi-billionaire. (1) Product: capitalize on hospitable, English-speaking, reasonably priced services and attractions like Boracay; fix the Manila airport (worst in Asia) and the Piatco imbroglio; improve sidewalks and tourist police. (2) Transportation: stop sacrificing national carriers to open skies -- no country in the world has succeeded in tourism by undermining its national airline; review domestic links and cruise ship facilities (a hotel exec reports cruises avoid PH due to customs/immigration friction). (3) Accommodation: great hotels exist but more rooms across price ranges are needed. (4) Facilitation: abolish the airport terminal fee; fix immigration and customs for cruise ships. (5) Marketing: synchronized with the product; foreign tourists plan years in advance; tour wholesalers take three years to include new destinations; 'Malaysia Truly Asia' was consistent for over five years before taking root -- PH must match that consistency and constancy.
